lines.trans: Denis, can you imagine, today I lost our flash drive.
Well that is fine, at least we were not fired.
I do not need any handouts from Katya.
Out of pride I will not stay here to work.
Wait, after all it was not Katya at all who did this.
I talked with the chef in person this morning.
Really, you asked the chef for us yourself?
Of course, because without you it will be boring here.
I think I understood everything perfectly right now.
You invited me to the cafe and lied.
Why are you looking at me so strangely right now?
Because I like you very much too.
Denis, I see you are not bored at all anymore!

examples.text: Позвать врача.
examples.trans: To call a doctor.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она машину совсем не заметила.
examples.trans: She did not notice the car at all.

examples.text: Денис, дыши спокойно, сейчас вызовем скорую.
examples.trans: Denis, breathe calmly, we will call an ambulance now.

examples.text: Всё нормально, я просто конфетой подавился.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, I just choked on a candy.

meanings.note: Indeclinable neuter noun from French 'café' (coffeehouse).

examples.text: Слушай, пойдём сейчас вместе в кафе.
examples.trans: Listen, let us go to a cafe together right now.

examples.text: Ты позвал меня в кафе и соврал.
examples.trans: You invited me to the cafe and lied.

examples.text: Звать клиентов в детское кафе.
examples.trans: Call customers into a children's café.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оврать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lied', paired with 'врать'.

examples.text: Ты позвал меня в кафе и соврал.
examples.trans: You invited me to the cafe and lied.

examples.text: Потому что я соврал про деньги.
examples.trans: Because I lied about the money.

examples.text: Он никогда не соврал друзьям.
examples.trans: He never lied to his friends.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: Почему мы сегодня оба такие стеснительные?
examples.trans: Why are we both so shy today?

examples.text: Почему в зале вообще нет музыки?
examples.trans: Why is there no music in the hall at all?

examples.text: Почему за спиной, никто ничего не скрывает.
examples.trans: Why behind your back, nobody is hiding anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Завтра ваша команда снова играет со Спартаком.
examples.trans: Tomorrow your team plays against Spartak again.

examples.text: Поставь завтра на Спартак пятьдесят тысяч.
examples.trans: Put fifty thousand on Spartak tomorrow.

examples.text: Прости, что сегодня утром так вышло.
examples.trans: Sorry that it turned out like this this morning.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Смотрите, тут открыта страничка вашей Елены Павловны.
examples.trans: Look, your Elena Pavlovna's page is open here.

examples.text: Быстро закрой эту страницу!
examples.trans: Close this page quickly!

examples.text: Ты не обижайся, но это очень странно.
examples.trans: Do not take offense, but that is very strange.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она машину совсем не заметила.
examples.trans: She did not notice the car at all.

examples.text: Алло, скорая, у нас тут авария.
examples.trans: Hello, ambulance, we have an accident here.

examples.text: Виктор, ты этот тонкий намёк понял?
examples.trans: Viktor, did you understand that subtle hint?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'look, watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Look what I've got.

examples.text: Я смотрю телевизор.
examples.trans: I'm watching TV.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.text: Я завтра утром женюсь, потом банкет.
examples.trans: I am getting married tomorrow morning, then the banquet.

examples.text: Может, она хочет потом квартиру себе забрать?
examples.trans: Maybe she wants to take the apartment for herself later?

examples.text: Потому что ты мне тоже очень нравишься.
examples.trans: Because I like you very much too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что тут непонятного, приезжайте скорее.
examples.trans: What is unclear here, come quickly.

examples.text: Что у тебя там в руках?
examples.trans: What do you have there in your hands?

examples.text: Что тебе нужно, говори быстрее.
examples.trans: What do you need, speak faster.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам тоже нужна статья!
examples.trans: We need an article too!

examples.text: Кстати, я тоже там у тебя в друзьях.
examples.trans: By the way, I am also on your friends list there.

examples.text: И за Свету тоже, она моя подруга.
examples.trans: And for Sveta too, she is my friend.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тут очень интересная статья про ресторан.
examples.trans: Here is a very interesting article about a restaurant.

examples.text: Елена, привет, я уже очень соскучился.
examples.trans: Elena, hello, I have missed you very much already.

examples.text: Прекрасно, тогда я тебя очень жду.
examples.trans: Wonderful, then I am waiting for you eagerly.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'appeal to, are liked', paired with 'понравиться'.

examples.text: Мне нравится кофе.
examples.trans: I like coffee.

examples.text: Людям нравится.
examples.trans: People like it.

examples.text: Реакция положительная. Людям нравится.
examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.text: Я просто совсем не ожидал увидеть.
examples.trans: I just did not expect to see at all.

examples.text: Всё чётко записано на моём видеорегистраторе.
examples.trans: Everything is clearly recorded on my dashcam.

examples.text: Стирай немедленно, пока Лена не увидела!
examples.trans: Erase it immediately before Lena sees it!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Елена, привет, я уже очень соскучился.
examples.trans: Elena, hello, I have missed you very much already.

examples.text: Точно, тебе обязательно нужен хороший врач.
examples.trans: Exactly, you definitely need a good doctor.

examples.text: Ну про Лёву ты уже всё знаешь.
examples.trans: Well, you already know everything about Lyova.

скучать.gloss: to miss, yearn for, feel bored

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'кучать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to miss, yearn for, feel bored', paired with 'соскучиться'.

examples.text: Денис, я вижу, ты уже совсем не скучаешь!
examples.trans: Denis, I see you are not bored at all anymore!

examples.text: Я буду очень скучать по вам.
examples.trans: I will miss you very much.

examples.text: Она скучает по родному городу.
examples.trans: She misses her hometown.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'правильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Подожди, ты неправильно всё поняла!
examples.trans: Wait, you misunderstood everything!

examples.text: Наше знакомство началось как-то неправильно.
examples.trans: Our acquaintance started somehow wrong.

examples.text: Подожди, ты совсем неправильно поняла.
examples.trans: Wait, you understood completely wrong.
